item.title: Trump Targets Muslim Brotherhood: US president to name some chapters as 'terrorist organisations'
item.description: President Trump has initiated the process to designate specific Muslim Brotherhood branches in Lebanon, Egypt, and Jordan as foreign terrorist organizations. The White House stated this move targets the group's network, which allegedly fuels terrorism and destabilizes regions impacting US interests and allies. This designation carries implications for asset freezes and travel bans.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Court quashes Comey and Letitia James cases: Trump’s interim attorney pick ruled invalid
item.description: A federal judge has dismissed indictments against James Comey and Letitia James, ruling President Trump's appointment of interim US attorney Lindsey Halligan invalid. The judge cited Halligan's "defective appointment" as unlawful, impacting all actions taken under her tenure. While charges can be refiled, Comey's may be time-barred. The Justice Department plans an appeal.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: These abandoned orcas in a French marine park are running out of time and every option looks grim
item.description: Two orcas remain trapped in algae-tainted tanks at the closed Marineland Antibes, with France’s legal deadline for relocation set for 2026, a timeline activists say the whales’ health cannot endure. Drone footage by Seph Lawless exposed the conditions and prompted urgent debate, yet every relocation option is stalled, rejected, unbuilt or bleak, leaving Wikie and Keijo running out of time.
item.dc:creator: TOI Trending Desk

item.title: False name, fake DOB: How Indian national wanted for murder got caught at US-Canada border through biometrics
item.description: A 22-year-old Indian national, Vishat Kumar, wanted for murder in India, was apprehended at the Canadian border. He attempted to enter Canada using a fake identity after illegally entering the US last year and missing an asylum interview. Biometrics led to his capture, and he now awaits extradition to India.

item.title: Trump Gold Card: $15,000 application fee to buy US residency for $1 million, draft petition ready ahead of December 18 deadline
item.description: The Trump administration is moving forward with its Gold Card visa program, set for a December 18 launch. Applicants can secure permanent residency by donating $1 million (or $2 million for corporations), with a $15,000 non-refundable fee. This will give applicants eligibility under EB-1 or EB-2 categories after a thorough vetting process.

item.title: Situation improved: US terminates Temporary Protected Status for Myanmar, asks Burmese nationals to go home
item.description: The Trump administration is ending Temporary Protected Status for Myanmar nationals, effective January 26, 2026. Citing improvements in governance and stability, Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem stated the situation is now safe for Burmese citizens to return home. This decision impacts nearly 4,000 individuals currently residing in the US under TPS.

item.title: Erika Kirk shares the real story behind her viral JD Vance hug and why she touched back of his head on stage
item.description: Erika Kirk defended a hug with Vice President JD Vance at a Turning Point USA event, stating it was a natural expression of her "love language is touch." The embrace, occurring shortly after the death of her husband Charlie Kirk, drew online scrutiny, but Kirk insists it was non-romantic and a gesture of comfort and pride.
item.dc:creator: Sehjal Gupta

item.title: 'Fallacy Vivek is peddling': Ramaswamy shares govt data on how American students fail in maths; gets slammed
item.description: GOP candidate Vivek Ramaswamy highlighted US government data showing a significant lack of math and reading proficiency among American students. While he argued for education reform, he got accused of 'Hindu supremacism' and 'American student bashing,' as all his arguments about US education system get tied to the H-1B storm that he triggered last Christmas by calling Americans lazy.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Man claims he’s ‘stranded’ on an island off the coast of Argentina, but is it real or staged for publicity?
item.description: William Banks has spent weeks claiming he’s stranded on an island off Argentina, posting survival-style footage and dramatic updates. But Banks is a Brooklyn-based method actor known for staged sagas, and the island narrative aligns closely with his upcoming boxing event in Buenos Aires on 20 December. The storyline increasingly appears to be a calculated performance rather than a genuine emergency.

item.title: Kash Patel 'furious' as SWAT team leaves his girlfriend Alexis Wilkins at a performance after 'no threat' assessment
item.description: Kash Patel ripped into the team's commander and said that he saw it as a failure in their communication that they left the event where Alexis Wilkins was performing --before the event ended. The agents claimed that they found the event site was secured and Kash Patel's girlfriend did not have any threat there.

item.title: Is Erika Kirk pregnant? Megyn Kelly reacts as Erika says she prayed for a baby when Charlie Kirk was killed
item.description: Erika Kirk, widow of conservative activist Charlie Kirk, revealed her profound grief and hope during a talk with Megyn Kelly. She shared her prayer of being pregnant at the time of Charlie's tragic death, desiring a larger family. Erika also urged young women to prioritize starting families, emphasizing that careers can wait, but motherhood cannot be indefinitely postponed.

item.title: 'Willing to provide...': Candace Owens doubles down on France-Charlie Kirk theory after Telegram CEO says it's entirely plausible
item.description: Conspiracy theorist Candace Owens claimed the French government is plotting her assassination, involving an Israeli and a French assassin, with payments being routed through a French club. Telegram CEO Pavel Durov supported Owens' theory, stating French intelligence is known for assassinations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Keenyah Hill threatens to sue Plaqueboymax after viral IRL stream encounter, model claims streamer ignored her request
item.description: Model Keenyah Hill is threatening legal action against Twitch streamer Plaqueboymax after an IRL stream interaction went viral. Hill claims she explicitly asked the streamer not to use footage of her asking for a "smooch," which he allegedly ignored. Plaqueboymax has since responded, stating he did not want to kiss her and is unfazed by the lawsuit threat.
